x: Rowpine has two parts. The rowpine npm package does the work: it reads your TanStack table and writes the files, and it builds pivots. The UI (an export menu, a pivot table and a pivot designer) comes from the shadcn registry, so its source lands in your project and picks up your theme. Terminal Copy export-menu installs components/export-menu.tsx . pivot installs components/pivot-table.tsx and co

href="#requirements" aria-label="Link to this section"># React 18 or 19 and a shadcn/ui project. Both shadcn bases work: Base UI, the default for new projects, and Radix. TanStack Table v8 ( useReactTable ) or v9 ( useTable ). Rowpine reads the table you pass it and does not add TanStack as a dependency, so installing it never changes your TanStack version.
href="#next" aria-label="Link to this section"># Add the export menu to a table, then set your license key .

Pass the table you already render to ExportMenu . It works with the object useReactTable (v8) or useTable (v9) returns. tsx Copy The menu offers Excel, PDF and CSV. Each file holds what the user is looking at: the visible columns in their order, every row that passes the current filter (on every page, not just the one on screen), in the current sort, with groups in place.

exportXlsx writes a real .xlsx workbook, not a CSV renamed. What you get in Excel: Numbers and dates are typed cells, so they sort, filter and sum. A Date value becomes an Excel date; the image shows one selected. The header row is bold and frozen. Column widths follow the widths on screen. Hidden columns are left out, pinned columns are frozen, groups become outline rows with SUBTOTAL formulas. t

href="#dates-stored-as-strings" aria-label="Link to this section"># A date only becomes an Excel date when the cell value is a Date . If your data has ISO strings, convert them in the accessor ( accessorFn: (r) => new Date(r.date) ), or they export as text.

By default an export holds every row that passes the table's filters, on every page, in the current sort. Paging is a screen concern; the file gets the whole result. The rows option changes that: rows Rows in the file "all" (default) Every filtered row, all pages, grouped and sorted as on screen. "page" Only the rows on the current page. "selected" Only the selected rows (needs TanStack's row sele

Excel and PDF need formats in different shapes, so a column can set both. Excel: numFmt . An Excel number format code. The cell stays a number (or date) and Excel shows it formatted, so totals and filters still work. ts Copy Date columns default to yyyy-mm-dd . Without numFmt a number uses Excel's General format. PDF: format . A PDF holds text, so give it the text you show on screen. Reusing the f

cellStyle colors a cell in the Excel and PDF files. It gets the cell value and the row's original data and returns a fill, a text color and bold, or undefined for a plain cell. ts Copy Use one function for the screen and the file, as above, so they cannot drift apart. Colors are hex strings ( #rrggbb ). To style whole rows, such as a total row, pass rowStyle to the export or the menu: ts Copy

The file has the columns the user can see, in the order they see them. A column hidden with TanStack's column visibility is left out. In the image, Country is hidden, so the file has no Country column. Columns pinned to the start come first, then the rest, then columns pinned to the end, as on screen. Display columns, the ones without an accessor such as selection checkboxes and row actions, are l

Columns pinned to the start (TanStack v9) or to the left (v8) are frozen in Excel, so they stay in view while the user scrolls right. The header row is always frozen. ts Copy In the image the thick line after column A is the frozen pane edge: Customer stays put. Columns pinned to the end are written last, after the other columns, and are not frozen. Excel can only freeze leading columns.

When the table is grouped with TanStack's grouping feature, the file keeps the groups. Each group row is written with its label and its aggregates, bold, on a light fill. The rows under it get an Excel outline level, one per grouping level. The bars and minus buttons on the left of the image are Excel's: users can collapse a region or a product there. Group rows sit above their rows, as on screen.

A group row's aggregates are written as live formulas over the rows below it, not as pasted numbers. If someone edits an amount in Excel, the group total updates. In the image, Europe's amount is =SUBTOTAL(9,E3:E52) . The range includes the product group rows inside Europe, and SUBTOTAL skips other SUBTOTAL cells, so nothing is counted twice. Column aggregationFn Formula sum SUBTOTAL(9, ...) mean

Rows nested with getSubRows export with their hierarchy. ts Copy Every row is exported, expanded or not, in tree order: a parent, then its children, then the next parent. In Excel each depth is an outline level , and in the PDF the first column is indented by depth. Parent rows are bold in both files. Their values are whatever your data holds for them; Rowpine does not add formulas to tree rows, b

In Excel, tree rows get one outline level per depth. In the image, Platform, Web and Data are level 1 under Engineering, and Analytics and Pipelines are level 2 under Data. The minus buttons on parent rows collapse their children in Excel. Excel shows up to 7 outline levels, so deeper trees are capped at level 7. The last line of the image is the notice an unlicensed export carries; see license ke

The header row is built from your column definitions: A string header is used as is. A function header cannot be written to a file, so set meta.rowpine.header ; otherwise the column id is used. Columns inside header groups get the group names joined with / . In the image, the pivot's Units column under the Q1 group becomes Q1 / Units . One header row keeps the sheet easy to filter and sort. Column

exportPdf lays the table out on pages: the header row repeats on every page, rows are separated by light lines, and the footer shows the date and "Page X of Y". The PDF looks like a shadcn/ui table: no header fill, no stripes, group rows in the muted gray. See colors to match your own theme. ts Copy Wide tables fit the page: with more than 8 columns the page turns landscape, the text shrinks down

Grouped tables print their group rows bold on a light fill, with their aggregates, above the rows they group. Nested groups and tree rows are indented in the first column, one step per level. The aggregate text uses the column's format , so a summed amount looks like the amounts under it: ts Copy Set the group row fill with subtotalColor : ts Copy

CSV export is free and needs no license key. ts Copy CSV is for data, not for looking at, so it differs from the Excel and PDF files on purpose: One line per data row. Group header rows are left out, and grouped-by values (the region of each order) are kept. Numbers have no thousands separators; dates are yyyy-mm-dd , or yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm:ss when they have a time. The file starts with a byte order

TanStack Table can group rows but has no pivot. Rowpine's pivot turns flat rows into a cross-tab: fields down the side, fields across the top, and aggregated values where they meet. tsx Copy Keep config stable (module scope or useMemo ); usePivot recomputes when it changes.

Several measures sit side by side. rowHeader Header of the first column. Default: the row fields joined with / . rowSubtotals Group rows carry subtotals. D

Each value in a pivot has an aggregation: agg Result sum Total of the numbers. avg Mean of the numbers. min , max Smallest and largest number. count Number of rows. countDistinct Number of different values. first , last The first or last value, in data order. The Total column only appears when there are column fields. Without any, the value columns already are the totals. Totals are computed from

Group rows in PivotTable have a chevron. Clicking it hides or shows the rows under the group. The group keeps its subtotal, so a collapsed pivot still adds up. The table keeps its own state, or you can control it: tsx Copy defaultCollapsed starts an uncontrolled table with every group closed. Collapsing is a view setting. Exports always hold every row, with groups as Excel outline rows the user ca

PivotDesigner lets users build the pivot themselves, the way they would in Excel: a field list on the left, four wells (Filters, Columns, Rows, Values) and the pivot under them. tsx Copy A field's kind decides where it can go: a dimension goes to Rows, Columns or Filters, a measure to Values or Filters. group sorts the field list under headings; format formats a measure's values; defaultAgg sets t

href="#props" aria-label="Link to this section"># Prop What it does data , fields The rows and the fields users can pick. layout , onLayoutChange Control the layout. Without them the designer starts with the first dimension in Rows and the first measure in Values. presets Saved layouts in the Presets menu. aggregators Aggregations offered on value chips. Def

Users move fields in three ways: Drag a field from the list into a well, or a chip from one well to another. Dragging a chip back to the field list removes it. Tick a field in the list to add it to its default well (Rows for a dimension, Values for a measure). Untick it to remove it from every well. Menus : a field's ... menu adds it to a well, and a chip's ... menu moves it, removes it, or clears

A field in the Filters well limits which rows the pivot counts. When a field is dropped there, its value list opens: untick the values to leave out. The filter icon on the chip turns to the accent color while it excludes anything. The list has a search box, Select all and Clear, and shows how many values pass. In the layout a filter is the list of values that pass, or null for all of them: ts Copy

A designer layout is plain JSON: json Copy Pass layouts as presets and they appear in the Presets menu: tsx Copy To let users save their own views, control the layout and store it wherever your app keeps settings: localStorage, your database, the URL. tsx Copy The saved views example keeps them in localStorage.

A pivot exports like any table. pivot.table is a table view of the pivot for the exporters: tsx Copy pivotRowStyle makes group, subtotal and grand total rows bold. In Excel, row groups become outline levels (the bars on the left of the image) and the column headers join the column groups with the measure: Q1 / Sum of Amount . t: Export TanStack Table to Excel with grouped rows
x: A grouped TanStack table is easy to read on screen: regions, products under them, a total on each group row. Export it with a CSV button and all of that is gone. The file has flat rows, no totals, and amounts stored as text. This guide builds a table grouped by region and product, adds an Export menu, and gets you an Excel file that keeps the structure: each grouping level is an Excel outline leve
